records.name: Philomusica Chorale
records.summary: An auditioned volunteer chorus in Chestnut Hill that rehearses on Monday evenings from September to May and performs concerts each season.
records.what_you_do: Sing in one of the four voice sections, learn the season's music, and perform at the season's concerts. Newcomers can sit in on a few rehearsals before deciding to audition.

schedule.text: Mondays 7 to 9:30 pm, September through May, in Widener Hall at the Presbyterian Church of Chestnut Hill. Mostly in person, with occasional Zoom sessions.

locations.label: Widener Hall, Presbyterian Church of Chestnut Hill

cost.text: Suggested contribution of $300 to $600 per singer each season, which covers music licensing, rehearsal space and concerts. The chorus says it does not turn away a successful auditioner for money reasons.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on philomusicachorale.org, or email philomusicaoffice@gmail.com, to request an audition time or a rehearsal visit.
first_step.basis: The site calls the audition friendly and low stress, says all voice types and ages are considered, and explains how to arrange an audition or a rehearsal visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: The audition is friendly and low stress: you sing a song of your choice, do some warm-ups, and sing an excerpt the music director sends ahead of time, with possibly a short sight-reading exercise. Monday rehearsals run 7 to 9:30 pm and include a break with snacks and conversation. The site says reading music matters, but it sometimes considers singers who read less well. It does not say how long the audition lasts.
first_visit_tips: Arrange your audition or rehearsal visit in advance, since the site asks visitors to request one first.
Choose one song you know well to sing, and plan to warm up before you audition.
Rehearsals are at Widener Hall in the Presbyterian Church of Chestnut Hill, on Germantown Avenue. Some sessions are on Zoom.
Ask early about the suggested contribution if cost is a concern, since the chorus says money does not stop a successful auditioner.

records.notes: Single-page site: the audition, FAQ and past events all sit on the home page, so the deep pass used that URL for both fetches. drop_in changed from true to false because the site asks visitors to arrange a rehearsal visit first. Status moved to active on the May 16, 2026 concert. Upcoming concerts listed on the page are January 30, 2027 and May 15, 2027. Audition length is not stated.

records.name: Physicians for Social Responsibility Pennsylvania
records.summary: Doctors, nurses, and other health workers who speak up about pollution, climate, and energy in Pennsylvania. They hold public webinars and virtual meetings, run air monitoring and watchdog projects, and organize action campaigns.
records.what_you_do: Join a virtual meeting or public webinar, sign up for the newsletter and action alerts, or help with a project such as air monitoring or the concerned health professionals group.

schedule.text: Virtual meetings and webinars are posted on the events page as they are scheduled. No regular weekly or monthly meeting time is stated.

cost.text: Event costs are not stated on the events page. Donations and sustaining memberships are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter, or register for a virtual meeting listed on the events page.
first_step.basis: The group describes its webinars and virtual meetings as public, each listed event has a sign-up button, and the site lists several ways to take part.
first_step.what_to_expect: Its events include online meetings and webinars, and some are in person. The listed Environmental Movement Community meeting on October 21, 2026 is online from 7 to 8 pm. The site does not say how many people attend or how long a typical event lasts.
first_visit_tips: Click the sign-up button on an event page, and check whether the event is online or in person before you register.
The events page has a Load More button, so click it to see later listings.

records.notes: The events page lists a second event, on November 3, 2026, that is in person in Pittsburgh. It is outside the area, so it is not used as a Philadelphia event. The events page does not say whether events are open to the public or need registration; the public description comes from the group's own site as recorded in tier 1. The Concerned Health Professionals group (CHP PA) is part of this group: it takes members through a Become a Member link, and the page gives no dues, meeting schedule or accessibility details. The site does not describe volunteer roles, so the hands_on role is a loose fit.

records.name: Plays & Players Theatre
records.summary: A membership collective of theatre people at 1714 Delancey Place. It runs public shows, comedy nights, open mics, readings and a gallery, and members produce some of the shows.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a show, comedy night or reading, come to an open mic, or join as a member to take part in the collective.

schedule.text: Monday Night Jazz and Caked-Up Comedy repeat about every two weeks. Many events start at 8 pm, often at Quig's Pub. The site lists each date.

cost.text: Tickets vary by show and are sold through links on the site. Yearly membership is $50 (Social), $100 (Artistic) or $250 (Cornerstone).

first_step.how: Buy a ticket through the link on a public show, comedy night or open mic listing on the site. To join as a member, fill out the membership application linked from the membership page.
first_step.basis: Shows, comedy nights and open mics are open to the public with posted dates and ticket links, and membership applications are reviewed by a committee each month.
first_step.what_to_expect: Many nights start at 8 pm at Quig's Pub, which is part of the building at 1714 Delancey Place, and shows are ticketed through links on the site. The site does not say how long a night runs, what the seating is like, or what to wear. Membership gives access to the pub and to member events.
first_visit_tips: Buy your ticket through the link on the event listing before you arrive.
The site does not give parking, transit or step-free access details, so plan your route to 1714 Delancey Place ahead of time.
If you want to join, compare the three membership tiers on the membership page first.

records.notes: The homepage lists dates without a year. The 2026 behind last_sign_of_life comes from the 2026 in a Spookeasy event link on the group's own site, since the page prints no year, so treat the October dates with that caveat. Membership tiers come from the membership page, which also prints no year. The site has no parking, entrance or step-free access details. Visiting companies on the calendar (dance, sketch, improv, stand-up, film) were not logged as leads because they are one-time bookings, not partner groups. 1812 Productions is said to be based in the building, but the site gives no URL for it, so it is not logged.

records.name: P'nai Or Philadelphia
records.summary: A congregation in West Mount Airy that meets in the Common Room of Summit Presbyterian Church. Its Saturday services include morning prayer and a Torah service, followed by a potluck lunch and a Zoom option.
records.what_you_do: Come to Saturday morning services in person or on Zoom, join the Torah service and breakout discussion, bring a dish to the potluck, or join the Zoom Torah study from home led by the rabbi.

schedule.text: Saturday mornings: Shabbat service from 10:30 am to noon, a Torah service with breakout discussion to 1 pm, then a potluck lunch, in person and on Zoom. A Zoom Torah study from home runs 9:15 to 10:15 am, and a Zoom Shabbas Shmooze is sometimes held at 2:30 pm.

cost.text: The site does not list membership dues or a charge for Shabbat services. For the High Holy Days it suggests a donation and accepts any amount.

access.notes: The regular Shabbat space has steps and is not immediately wheelchair accessible. High Holy Day services may be held in Fellowship Hall, which has a ramp at the Westview Street entrance. Nearest SEPTA: Upsal Station on the Chestnut Hill West Regional Rail line, about 3 blocks away, and the H bus stops about 1 block away. The visit page names Rabbi Marcia Prager as the contact for access help.

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday morning service, in person or on Zoom. For the Zoom Torah study, read the Torah Study info sheet linked on the site first.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome, including people who are not Jewish and people with questions or doubts, and it explains how a newcomer can join the Zoom Torah study.
first_step.what_to_expect: The prayer style is lively and participatory, mixing Hebrew and English songs with time for reflection. The Shabbat service runs from 10:30 am to about 1 pm, and a potluck lunch follows. New people can join the Zoom Torah study from home, which runs 9:15 to 10:15 am, after reading its info sheet.
first_visit_tips: Enter by the Greene Street entrance. Look for the large sign on the lawn, go to the end of the walkway, and enter through the two red doors. Go down the steps, through the double doors, turn right, and the Common Room is the first door on your left.
Do not park on the 500 block of Westview next to the church, out of respect for the neighbors.
The Chestnut Hill West train has reduced weekday service and no weekend service, so on a Saturday take the H bus, which stops about one block away.
Bring a dish to share for the potluck lunch after the service, if you can.

records.notes: The homepage is the current source: it carries the High Holydays 5787/2026 label and an October 3 Saturday service. Several subpages are old: the join page links a 5775 membership form, and the learn page describes a 2015 study session and a different teacher for the Torah study. Times and names here come from the homepage only. The year behind last_sign_of_life 2026-10 is the one printed in the High Holydays 5787/2026 label. Membership dues are not stated. The visit page does not say visitors must register; only the High Holy Days need Eventbrite registration. Keshet, the network the congregation names as its affiliation, was not logged: it is not in this batch and is named only as an affiliation. Tier 1 said Community Wing; the visit page says Common Room, so the summary and location are corrected.

records.name: Polish People's University
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that has offered free lectures on Polish history, culture and tradition for more than 100 years. Anyone can attend the monthly talks from October to April at the Associated Polish Home, and some talks are also offered on Zoom.
records.what_you_do: Attend a monthly lecture, watch past talks on the group's YouTube channel, or join the mailing list for event news. The sign-up form may not be working yet.

schedule.text: Monthly lectures from October to April, usually at 3 pm. Most are held at the Associated Polish Home on Academy Road, and some are offered on Zoom.

cost.text: Lectures are free. Donations are welcome and are tax deductible.

first_step.how: Come to the next lecture at the Associated Polish Home, 9150 Academy Road, at 3 pm. For the Zoom option, email the group first, since the site does not say how to get the link.
first_step.basis: The site says all lectures are free and open to everyone, and it gives the address, the lecture times and a contact email.
first_step.what_to_expect: A lecture is one talk on one topic, starting at 3 pm. Topics run from Polish history and art to medicine and technology, and each lecture has a named speaker. The site does not say how long a talk runs or whether there is time for questions.
first_visit_tips: Check the lectures page for the month's talk, and whether it is in person or on Zoom.
The site does not describe parking or nearby transit for the Associated Polish Home, so plan your route ahead of time.
Donations are welcome and tax deductible, but you do not need to give to attend.

records.notes: Lecture dates on the lectures page run from October 11, 2026 to April 18, 2027, each at 3 pm, and the page prints the year on each one. The mailing list form says it still needs a storage option, so sign-up may not work yet; what_you_do now says so. Zoom is offered for some lectures only, so the summary no longer says every talk is online. The Associated Polish Home is the venue; the site does not name a SEPTA stop, parking or step-free access, so no transit line is recorded. The contact page lists no phone or hours. The YouTube channel named in what_you_do comes from tier 1 and was not confirmed in this pass.

records.name: Practice Gallery
records.summary: An artist-run contemporary art gallery at 319 North 11th Street. Members choose the shows together, and the space is open to visitors on First Fridays, on Saturdays and Sundays from 2 to 6 pm, and by appointment.
records.what_you_do: See the shows during public hours or at a First Friday opening. Artists who want to join the governing group can follow the New Member Call page and apply.

schedule.text: Open to visitors on First Fridays, on Saturdays and Sundays from 2 to 6 pm, and by appointment. New shows are posted on the site as they open.

cost.text: Admission is not stated on the site. Members of the governing group share rent and utilities, usually about $100 a month.

first_step.how: Visit during public hours or at a First Friday opening, or email info@practicegallery.org to book another time. To ask about joining the governing group, send the email described on the New Member Call page with a letter of intent.
first_step.basis: Public hours and openings are open to anyone, and the site lists how to book a visit. Joining the governing group takes a written application.
first_step.what_to_expect: During public hours you can look at the current show at your own pace. On First Fridays the gallery holds openings. The site does not say how long a visit takes or whether staff are on hand.
first_visit_tips: Check the site for the current show and its run dates before you go.
Go during public hours, or email ahead to book a time on other days.
The site does not describe stairs, an elevator or step-free access, so email ahead if access matters to you.
The New Member Call page lists an October 25 deadline with no year printed, so confirm the current round before you apply.

records.notes: The earlier claim of a new show about once a month is not stated on the site, so the summary no longer makes it; the listings show roughly one exhibition a month, which is a reading of the list, not a stated schedule. The New Member Call deadline is October 25 with no year printed, so it is not recorded as a dated item. The listing labels marked Practice are post dates, not openings, so only the First Friday opening and the July 10 to August 7, 2026 run are used. painting_drawing is the closest tag for a contemporary art gallery; the gallery's focus is performance and participation, which the tag does not capture. Admission is not stated.

records.name: Precious Gems Supportive Services
records.summary: A community nonprofit that helps children and teens cope with grief, loss, and big life changes. Its programs give young people room to grieve and healthy ways to express what they feel.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the teen or children's grief programs. Call or email the office to ask how to enroll.

schedule.text: Meeting times for the children's and teen programs are not posted on the site.

locations.label: Office
locations.address: 231 South Easton Road, Second Floor, Glenside, PA 19038

cost.text: Cost is not stated on the site.

access.notes: The office is on the second floor of the Glenside building. The site does not say whether there is an elevator.

first_step.how: Call 215-224-5655 or email info@preciousgems.org to ask about the teen and children's programs and how to enroll.
first_step.basis: The site names the teen and children's programs and gives a phone number and email, but it does not say how to enroll, which ages are served, or whether there is a fee.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first session, group size, or where youth groups meet. Call the office to ask about age ranges, how a group meets, and what it costs. The wider services include time-limited support groups led by grief professionals and referrals to counseling and community groups.
first_visit_tips: Call before you visit, since the site does not list office hours.
Ask on the first call about age ranges, meeting times and cost, because the site does not state them.
The office is on the second floor, so ask ahead about stairs or an elevator if that matters.

records.notes: Verdict stays publish, but the service area is unclear. The group's own pages give a Glenside office and a Philadelphia PO box, and do not say which places it serves. A web search returned a summary that says it serves Philadelphia and nearby Montgomery County, but that summary came from a leads-only listing and was not checked against the group's own pages, so nothing from it is recorded. The owner should decide whether a Glenside-based group belongs in a Philadelphia directory. The group's own site shows no dated news, so status stays probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is set. No ages, enrollment steps or fees are published. Uplift Center for Grieving Children was named in a search result but had no usable URL, so it is not logged.

leads_only.name: Peter's Place
leads_only.note: Peer grief support for children, teens and caregivers, found in a 211 directory listing during the search. This is a directory page, not the group's own website, and it was not checked further.

notes: Batch held 7 groups, all processed. Verdicts: publish 7, hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Fetches used 21 of 60 allowed, with at most 4 per group. WebSearch used 1 of 1; its result added no recorded facts. No blocked pages or rate limits. Corrections to tier 1: P'nai Or meets in the Common Room, not the Community Wing; Polish People's University offers Zoom for some lectures only; Practice Gallery shows are not on a stated monthly schedule; Philomusica drop_in set to false because visitors must arrange a rehearsal visit; the Philomusica and P'nai Or statuses are now active on 2026 dated evidence; the dated event was removed from the PSR schedule text. Open questions for the owner: (1) Precious Gems is based in Glenside, outside the city, and its own pages do not state a service area. (2) P'nai Or's subpages are old, so only the homepage was used for times and names. Not logged: Keshet (named by P'nai Or as its affiliation), 1812 Productions and the visiting performers at Plays & Players, and the Associated Polish Home (venue only, no URL on the site). Records were written by hand; the summaries were not copied from any source.
